text:
deploy-bot: rollout started for service=router version=v2 -> canary(10%) at 1965432100. commit=9f3b2a1. feature_flag=new-routing-ff. details: https://ci.internal/runs/9876
sophia: ack, I'm on the canary. trying to pull up the per-canary latency dashboard but the 'canary-latency' dashboard returns 404 for me. anyone else?
jordan: seeing spike on /generate error rate ~3x baseline, 502/504s from model-proxy in traces. SLO burn windows show +12% error budget in last 5m.
deploy-bot: ALERT: deploy_canary_error_rate firing (prometheus) — paging oncall
oncall-bot: Paging @sophia (severity=high) — please ack and investigate :rotating_light:
sophia: acked. investigating. first checks: logs, kill-switch path, rollback playbook. if needed we can flip new-routing-ff off.
sophia: command I will use if needed: 
```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"flag":"new-routing-ff","enabled":false}'
```
pranav: I can flip it from the flags console too. before we do that, can we confirm it's the routing change? logs show an NPE in router/shard_map at the same time the canary got traffic.
jordan: confirmed customer-facing impact: 3 support tickets in EU region reporting 503/timeout. I'm starting a customer-impact note.
customer-success: adding detail: customers ACME and BetaCorp reporting degraded throughput and periodic 503s since 23:00 UTC. They've escalated to P1 and want updates.
sophia: traces show model-proxy returning timeouts -> upstream 504. dashboard for canary-specific metrics is missing (looks like the dashboard templating job didn't tag dashboards for this release). hard to correlate quickly without it.
leo: I can restore the dashboard from snapshot but first we should stop the canary if traffic is harming customers. recommend kill flag then restore dashboards.
pranav: flipping flag now (console). route will be reverted to v1.
pranav: `200 OK` — flag new-routing-ff disabled. traces now show traffic routed back to router v1, canary traffic down to ~0%.
deploy-bot: rollback action detected: operator=pranav triggered rollback at 1965432222. canary traffic -> 0%.
jordan: error rate dropping already, SLO burn trending back down but we still have noisy alerts firing from both canary-specific and global rules. duplicates causing alert fatigue.
sophia: agreed. temporary mitigation: silence canary-specific alert group and add a short silence for the duplicate global rule. runbook snippets: 
- silence canary alerts: `curl -XPOST https://alertmanager.internal/api/v1/silences -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"deploy_canary_errors"}],"startsAt":"...","endsAt":"...","createdBy":"sophia"}'`
- add global silence for the duplicate noise window in alertmanager UI
oncall-bot: Silence created for alert group deploy_canary_errors for 30m by sophia.
eng-infra: quick note — the dashboard templating job failed because the CI runner lost write perms to dashboards-bucket when we rotated a service account yesterday. I'll patch the CI job and backfill the missing dashboards.
pranav: follow-ups: 1) confirm dashboard CI fix + backfill, 2) dedupe alerting rules so canary/global don't both fire, 3) add automated kill-switch rollback if error budget burn > 8% in 3m for canary.
jordan: customer-impact doc: https://incidents.internal/1965432100-impact — listing affected customers, tickets, and timeline.
leo: taking handoff at 23:30 UTC. I'll monitor overnight and coordinate postmortem. added runbook links to the incident doc.
customer-success: thanks — telling customers ACME and BetaCorp that we've rolled back and are monitoring; will follow up once postmortem is ready.
sophia: creating incident stub and postmortem outline now. primary remediation items: restore dashboard CI perms, alert dedupe, and automate kill-switches + better canary observability.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: from sophia to leo at 1965432387.
